tyler-tanner: Wonderkid. Starboy. Hometown hero. Whatever you want to call him, Tanner is one of the best players in the nation. The Brentwood, Tennessee, native was recently named to the preseason AP All-America team — and for good reason.

As a sophomore, Tanner averaged 19.5 points, 5.1 assists and 2.4 steals per game. Better yet, in conference play alone, his averages jumped to 21.5 points, 5.5 assists and 2.3 steals — making him the only SEC player in the last 30 seasons to surpass the 21/5/2 marks. He received just about every accolade you could think of: All-SEC first team, SEC All-Defensive team and AP All-America honorable mentions from the Associated Press and USBWA.

The 6-foot guard set single-season Vanderbilt records in total steals (86) and total assists (184). He also became just the second player in Commodore history to score over 700 points in a season (702). In short, there isn't much that Tanner hasn't proved so far. He is one of the top contenders for the National Player of the Year award, and without a doubt the leader of this team.
ace-glass: Glass brings an impressive arsenal of three-level scoring from Washington State.
bangot-dak: Dak’s athletic build gives him the potential to be an elite rim-running, lob-catching and shot-blocking big man for the ’Dores.
chandler-bing: The second of three returners on the roster, Bing showed serious flashes of potential as a significant contributor during his freshman season.
sebastian-williams-adams: Williams-Adams was highly recruited by Byington and the Vanderbilt staff — and nearly committed to the Black and Gold straight out of high school. Instead, he joined the Auburn Tigers in their first season under head coach Steven Pearl.
berke-buyuktuncel: In an unprecedented move in the college basketball world, Buyuktuncel joined the Commodores over the summer after his former team, Nebraska, took down Vanderbilt in one of the best March Madness games in recent memory.
t-o-barrett: Barrett had a few breakout games last season with Missouri but was behind Anthony Robinson and star guard/forward Mark Mitchell in the rotation.
jayden-leverett: As a freshman, Leverett saw his minutes increase throughout the season. He made the most of this playing time, impacting the game through hustle plays and strong effort.
ant-brown-jr: Brown has made the most of his opportunities through three exhibition games thus far — particularly against UAB, when he dropped a double-double with 10 points and 10 assists.
gabe-nesmith: After reclassifying from 2027 to 2026, Nesmith followed in his cousin Aaron Nesmith’s footsteps and came to play for the Commodores.
